hints.title: Keep the original sign condition
hints.body: A square root is nonnegative. Before changing the equation, work out what that requires of the other side.
hints.recap: The original equation imposes a sign restriction as well as a square-root domain.
hints.pitfall: Squaring can make opposite signs look equal.
hints.pause: Write the sign restriction and compare it with the proposed roots.

recall.reminder: Keep conditions from the original equation when a transformation may add solutions.

hints.title: Test the candidates before blaming a step
hints.body: For each proposed root, evaluate the left and right sides of the original equation separately. Then work backwards through the displayed equations.
hints.recap: A solution of a transformed equation must still satisfy the original one.
hints.pitfall: A correct expansion does not repair a condition lost earlier.
hints.pause: Locate the first pair of consecutive lines that do not have exactly the same solutions.

recall.reminder: Check each implication in both directions when the argument claims equivalent equations.

solution:
x=−1 satisfies the original equation, but x=−4 gives 1=−1, which is false. Thus exactly one of the proposed solutions is correct.

Squaring in Step 1 discards the requirement x+3≥0. The later algebra correctly solves the squared equation, but its roots must be checked in the original one. Answer C.
knowledgePattern: Locate loss of equivalence when squaring
